title: An ample line induces an isogeny over any field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], and choose a normalized dual Poincare datum $(A^\vee,\mathcal P_A)$ [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum]. Let $L$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_A$-module [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module, def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $\phi_L:A\to A^\vee$ be the group-scheme homomorphism [def-sc-group-scheme] classifying the normalized difference $N_L$ of that datum, so $(1\times\phi_L)^*\mathcal P_A\simeq N_L$ with its identity-axis rigidification. Then $\phi_L$ is an isogeny [def-sc-isogeny]: it is surjective and its scheme-theoretic kernel is finite over $k$. No separability of the isogeny, perfection of $k$, or restriction on its characteristic is assumed.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1 (ample implies zero-dimensional translation kernel), printed p.35; Proposition 8.14 and the normalized-difference construction, printed pp.39–40; §11 opening definition of polarization, printed p.53. Arbitrary-field formulation includes scheme-theoretic kernels.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/k$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and put $X=A_\Omega$, $D=(A^\vee)_\Omega$, and $M=L_\Omega$. By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], both $A$ and $A^\vee$ are geometrically integral; hence $X,D$ are connected and integral by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Properness and smoothness survive this base change by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Their group operations base change by the fibre-product universal property, so $X,D$ are abelian varieties. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to see that $M$ is absolutely ample. The hypotheses are satisfied because the only nonempty affine open of either field spectrum is the whole spectrum.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1 and Remark 8.2, printed p.35; Proposition 8.14 and normalized difference, printed pp.39–40. Reduction to a positive power with a section and fpqc descent are written out by Q98.

proof.text: The pulled-back Poincare module $P_\Omega$ on $X\times_\Omega D$ represents the same normalized functor over $\Omega$: for any $\Omega$-scheme $T$, regard $T$ as a $k$-scheme and identify $X\times_\Omega T=A\times_kT$. Its identity rigidification and its geometric-fibre algebraic triviality are exactly the conditions in [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum]. The unique classifying $k$-map $T\to A^\vee$, paired with the structural map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, is a unique $\Omega$-map $T\to D$. The tensor group law also pulls back: the group structure of $D(T)$ is that of $A^\vee(T)$, so the tensor product of the families classified by $u,v:T\to D$ is classified by $u+v$. Let $E$ and $\mathcal P_X$ be the dual and Poincare sheaf of $X$ in [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus]. Applying the two universal properties to the universal families gives $\Omega$-morphisms $\psi:D\to E$ with $(1\times\psi)^*\mathcal P_X\simeq P_\Omega$ and $\chi:E\to D$ with $(1\times\chi)^*P_\Omega\simeq\mathcal P_X$, both respecting rigidifications. They are inverse because their composites classify the original universal families. The identity $0_D$ classifies $P_\Omega|_{X\times0}$, which is trivial by the datum, and $0_E$ classifies the trivial family by the normalization of $\mathcal P_X$ on $X\times0$; uniqueness gives $\psi(0_D)=0_E$. No compatibility of $\psi$ with the group laws is used below: [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] does not identify the addition of $E$ with tensor product, so all additive arguments are made in $D$. Write $f:X\to D$ for $(\phi_L)_\Omega$. The pullback-composition and tensor comparisons [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition, lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] give $N_L|_{X\times X}=N_M$ including the constant identity-line factor. Thus $f$ classifies $N_M$ in $D$, with its rigidification.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1 and Remark 8.2, printed p.35; Proposition 8.14 and normalized difference, printed pp.39–40. Reduction to a positive power with a section and fpqc descent are written out by Q98.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base] to $X/\Omega$ and $M$. It gives $d\ge1$ and an immersion $i:X\to\mathbf P^r_\Omega$ with $H:=M^{\otimes d}\simeq i^*\mathcal O(1)$. We also verify the complete-linear-system convention of [def-sc-ample]. By [lem-fin-proper-coherent-finite-dimensional], $V=H^0(X,H)$ is finite dimensional; invertibility makes $H$ coherent since $X$ is finite type over the field. The last clause of [lem-trf-relative-ample-very-ample], applied to the relatively very ample $H$ and the quasi-compact structure map of the proper $X$, says that the evaluation quotient is surjective and that its associated complete-system map $j:X\to\mathbf P(V)$ is an immersion. This projective space is separated by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. Since $X$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $j$ proper. An immersion is a monomorphism, so [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] makes $j$ a closed immersion. Hence $H$ is very ample, and therefore ample in [def-sc-ample].

source.place: I Proposition 8.1 and Remark 8.2, printed p.35; Proposition 8.14 and normalized difference, printed pp.39–40. Reduction to a positive power with a section and fpqc descent are written out by Q98.

proof.text: The global generation of $H$ in step 3 and the identity point of the nonempty $X$ give a nonzero section $s\in H^0(X,H)$: if every section were zero, evaluation at that point could not generate its one-dimensional fibre. As $X$ is integral, [lem-pc-nonzero-section-integral-cartier] makes $F=Z(s)$ an effective Cartier divisor. By [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso], $H\simeq\mathcal O_X(F)$. Apply the effective-divisor criterion in [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] to $X,F$: step 3 verified its ampleness hypothesis in precisely its complete-system convention. Thus the homomorphism $\phi_H=\phi_{\mathcal O_X(F)}:X\to E$ is surjective and has finite scheme-theoretic kernel. Let $g:X\to D$ be the map classifying $N_H$ in $D$ (step 2). Then $\psi\circ g$ classifies $(1\times g)^*P_\Omega\simeq N_H$ in $E$, so $\psi\circ g=\phi_H$ by uniqueness. As $\psi$ is an isomorphism with $\psi(0_D)=0_E$, $g$ is surjective and $\ker g=X\times_{D,g,0_D}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=X\times_{E,\phi_H,0_E}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=\ker\phi_H$ is finite. This also covers the empty divisor on a zero-dimensional abelian variety.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1 and Remark 8.2, printed p.35; Proposition 8.14 and normalized difference, printed pp.39–40. Reduction to a positive power with a section and fpqc descent are written out by Q98.

proof.text: Expand the four factors of the normalized difference from [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum]. Pullback distributes over tensor product by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor], and the dual of a tensor power of a line is its inverse tensor power (checked on a local generator and evaluation). Consequently $N_H=N_{M^{\otimes d}}\simeq N_M^{\otimes d}$ with the identity-axis trivialization; the constant factor is $(0^*M)^{\otimes d}$ on both sides. The datum's tensor group law in $D$ (step 2) says that the family on the right is classified by the $d$-fold sum $f+\dots+f=[d]_D\circ f$ in $D(X)$. Its uniqueness therefore gives $g=[d]_D\circ f$. Since $f=(\phi_L)_\Omega$ is a group homomorphism, repeated addition also gives $[d]_D\circ f=f\circ[d]_X$. These are identities of morphisms, obtained from rigidified families, not only identities on geometric points.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1 and Remark 8.2, printed p.35; Proposition 8.14 and normalized difference, printed pp.39–40. Reduction to a positive power with a section and fpqc descent are written out by Q98.

proof.text: Surjectivity of $g=f\circ[d]_X$ implies surjectivity of $f$: a point in the image of $g$ is the image under $f$ of the corresponding point under $[d]_X$. Let $K=\ker f$ and $K_d=\ker g$. By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], both are closed subgroup schemes of $X$. The equality $g=[d]_D\circ f$ gives a factorization $K\to K_d$ of their closed immersions into $X$. This is a closed immersion: locally in $X$, the ideals satisfy $I_{K_d}\subseteq I_K$, so the induced map is the quotient by $I_K/I_{K_d}$. Since $K_d$ is finite over $\Omega$, it is affine with finite-dimensional coordinate algebra by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; its closed subscheme $K$ has a quotient coordinate algebra, still finite dimensional, and is therefore finite. Nilpotents are retained in this quotient argument; reducedness of either kernel is not used.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1 and Remark 8.2, printed p.35; Proposition 8.14 and normalized difference, printed pp.39–40. Reduction to a positive power with a section and fpqc descent are written out by Q98.

proof.text: The singleton $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is an fpqc covering in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: it is flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat], and the one affine source covers the one-point target. Its pullback $D\to A^\vee$ is an fpqc covering, hence surjective, by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. By step 2, $f$ is exactly $(\phi_L)_\Omega$, so step 6 proves this base-changed homomorphism surjective. For any point $y\in A^\vee$ choose a point of $D$ over it and then a preimage under $(\phi_L)_\Omega$; its projection to $A$ maps to $y$. Thus $\phi_L$ is surjective. Moreover the kernel fibre product commutes with this scalar extension: $(A\times_{A^\vee,\phi_L,0}\operatorname{Spec}k)_\Omega=X\times_{D,(\phi_L)_\Omega,0}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, by the universal property of the two fibre products [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup]. Step 6 makes the latter finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] to the former kernel's structure map and the same fpqc covering to conclude that $\ker\phi_L$ is finite over $k$.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1 and Remark 8.2, printed p.35; Proposition 8.14 and normalized difference, printed pp.39–40. Reduction to a positive power with a section and fpqc descent are written out by Q98.

proof.text: The given $\phi_L$ is a group-scheme homomorphism, and step 7 supplies surjectivity and finiteness of its scheme-theoretic kernel. These are exactly the two requirements of [def-sc-isogeny]. The algebraic-closure reduction used neither perfectness of $k$ nor a prime-to-characteristic tensor exponent; the quotient-algebra and fpqc arguments allow nonreduced kernels.
